caption:
On 60 Minutes, Trump said AI risk can be managed, and that the DOJ can do it.
His example: someone at "one of the big" AI companies was told to get ready to go to jail.
He would not name the person or the company, and said he doesn't mind guardrails as long as the US stays ahead of China.

Should the government be able to threaten AI bosses with jail?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: CBS News, Reuters · Photo: radaronline.com
threads_text: Trump told 60 Minutes the DOJ warned someone at one of the big AI companies to get ready to go to jail, and that the person then changed everything. He won't say who. Is that how AI should be regulated?

slides.headline: Trump says the DOJ warned a top AI boss: *get ready to go to jail*

slides.heading: A warning *before bedtime*

slides.heading: "I don't mind *guardrails*"

His condition: no rules that put the US in "a deep second position" behind China. In September he said a strong president was the only guardrail AI needed.

site_article.headline: Trump says the Justice Department warned an AI company leader of possible jail time

site_article.seo_title: Trump on 60 Minutes: DOJ warned AI company leader of jail
site_article.seo_description: Trump told 60 Minutes the DOJ warned someone at a major AI company to expect jail, and said he is open to AI guardrails if the US stays ahead of China.
site_article.answer_summary: Trump said the Justice Department can manage AI risk and described an unnamed case in which someone at one of the big AI companies was told to get ready for jail. He did not say who it was or what the person had done.

paragraphs.text: President Donald Trump said in an interview with CBS's 60 Minutes, aired on November 8, 2026, that the risks of artificial intelligence can be managed and that the Justice Department is one of the ways to manage them. In the same conversation he described a case in which, by his account, a person at a major AI company was warned to prepare for jail.

According to the transcript published by CBS News, Trump said someone had been reported to the administration for doing something bad with AI. He said the person was called and told to go home, see their family and kiss them good night, because they would be going to jail the next morning. Trump said the person then changed course completely.

Trump declined to identify the person or the company. Asked whether it was the leader of a major AI company, he answered that it was one of the big ones. He added that he did not think the conduct had been malicious, though he said it could have been. The transcript does not give a date, a name or a description of what the person allegedly did.
FourWeekMBA, which reviewed the transcript, noted that the account rests only on the president's words and that it found no other public record of such a warning.

During the interview, the questioner noted that people in the AI industry have put the chance that the technology could kill humanity at around 10 percent. Trump replied that the risk is not nearly as real as such warnings suggest and that it can be managed.

Reuters reported that Trump signaled openness to safeguards, quoting him as saying he does not mind guardrails. He said he did not want rules that would put the United States in a deep second position behind China, which he said has no such restrictions. Asked whether he would work with Democrats on AI rules, he said he absolutely would. Reuters noted that Trump has generally favored letting technology companies police themselves and that it remains unclear what level of safeguards he would accept.

The comments are a change in tone from September 2026, when Trump wrote on Truth Social that the only guardrail AI needs is a strong and smart president, according to Startup Fortune. The outlet also reported that House Democrats, who won a majority in the midterm elections, plan to hold hearings on AI after the new Congress is seated, with no dates set.

Trump also said companies building data centers must build their own power plants, and that excess electricity would flow into the grid. He described data centers as a source of money for the communities that host them, according to the CBS transcript.

The jail remark is the most striking part of the interview, but it comes without any detail that would allow it to be checked. If the account is accurate, it would mean the administration has used the threat of prosecution informally to change the behavior of a leading AI company, a different approach from the written rules lawmakers are discussing.

Watch whether the White House, the Justice Department or any AI company comments on the case Trump described, and whether his openness to guardrails turns into support for specific bills once the new Congress begins work.
